newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik peace talks suspended for two days.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace talks suspended for two days.

text.p: Tajikistan's Islamic opposition suspended peace talks with the Tajik government in Moscow for two days on Monday after one opposition member was killed and other five seized in the Tajik capital Dushanbe, Interfax news agency said.
It said the Afghan-based opposition had been outraged by the killing and the arrest of its members accused of involvement in a series of terrorist acts.

The Moscow-backed government said the incident occurred on February 24 when its forces tried to seize five of field commander Kasim Ismatov 's men who they believe were responsible for killing 42 government officials and Russian peacekeepers over the last two years.
The opposition denied any involvement in the terrorist acts and demanded a proper investigation in the incident.

The Moscow talks began last Wednesday. They are aimed at working out military arrangements to support a U.N.-sponsored peace accord signed last December after four years of fierce civil war in the former Soviet republic.
But they have stalled over plans to reintegrate armed opposition units into Tajikistan's military structures.
The talks are mediated by Russia, which has a large military presence in the remote Central Asian republic of 5.7 million people.

A ceasefire has largely been holding in Tajikistan since the December accord but Western observers say the two sides' inability to control armed bands who roam the mountainous state may jeopardise peace efforts.

Diplomats say a power-sharing deal recently struck in Iran, in which seats on a new commission for national reconciliation were shared out between the government and opposition, could be explosive because it leaves no places for any other faction.
